summary: Gate 1 (change summary), Gate 2 (security-guardian + docs-writer mandatory pair), and Gate 3 (architect + sre, routed-concerns row 38 Postgres-substrate trigger) ran on the base F031/F032/F033 implementation before this session's context was compacted; their specific findings are not re-derived here to avoid fabricating detail from an unavailable transcript. What is directly verified in this ledger: (1) at least one Gate 2 security-guardian finding was real and fixed live within this session (see pass_ordinal 2 below, the duplicate-item-id compensation gap), so Gate 2 ran and found a genuine defect, not a rubber-stamp; (2) the full pre-compaction transcript is recoverable at need per this repo's own 'Gov transcript recovery' convention (session JSONL under ~/.claude/projects), not reconstructed from memory here.

trigger: POST /api/product-packs with a bundle whose two documents share the same item_id
summary: The pre-existing duplicate-item-id check returned before compensate_fn ran, orphaning items install_fn already committed — the exact bug F031 exists to close, reached via a different trigger than the final-persist path.

trigger: New Idempotency-Key-too-long 400 check added with no audit_fn call
summary: Investigated as a possible code gap; verified the SAME handler already skips audit_fn on the pre-existing store-not-open (503) and invalid-JSON (400) checks — a pre-existing convention, not introduced by this PR. Fixed the DOC claim to accurately describe existing + new behavior rather than adding an inconsistent one-off audit call.

trigger: Two concurrent installs of the IDENTICAL bundle, no Idempotency-Key needed
summary: PolicyStore's own duplicate-name/PK check makes the second racer's PolicyFragment creation fail while its Policy's fragment lookup then matches the FIRST racer's already-committed fragment by id/name — a pack whose Policy depends on an unrelated, untracked pack's Fragment. NOT caught by compensate_and_fail (a per-item install_fn partial-success case, not a duplicate-id or final-persist failure). Verified pre-existing: install_fn's loop and PolicyStore's name-collision handling are byte-unchanged by this PR (git diff against origin/dev). Not fixed in this PR — flagged for the operator's explicit disposition rather than silently deferred or silently fixed, per the same standard the F031/F032/F033 findings themselves were originally deferred under.

trigger: A caller-supplied compensate_fn throws instead of returning false
summary: install() had no try/catch anywhere; a throwing compensate_fn would skip the rest of the reverse-order compensation loop, the compensation-outcome metric, and (via the caller's unwound stack) workflow_routes.cpp's audit_fn call — silently, unlike every failure path pre-PR which always reached audit_fn uninterrupted. Distinguished from #3482 (install_fn's own, pre-existing, explicitly-deferred exception-boundary gap): this specific call site (compensate_fn inside compensate_and_fail) is new in this PR.

trigger: Two concurrent installs racing the same not-yet-used Idempotency-Key with genuinely different bodies
summary: The loser of this specific race hits the persist INSERT's unique-violation (db_error/503, retryable) rather than the pre-check's differing-body 400 (non-retryable) — violates the hpp's documented "never kProductPackDbErrorPrefix for a differing-body key reuse" claim inside this narrow window; converges to the correct 400 on client retry. No data corruption, doc-accuracy only.

trigger: Client retries an install after a partial compensation failure
summary: A retry re-runs install_fn over the whole bundle rather than repairing just the residual item. Initially documented (changelog) as producing simple 'duplicate content'; corrected later in the session (enterprise-readiness Gate 6 finding) to name the sharper PolicyFragment/explicit-id case, where the outcome is silently MISSING content reported as success, not a duplicate.
disposition: partially fixed (doc corrected); the underlying design question is deferred to the operator, see enterprise-f1 below

trigger: rest-api.md described the Idempotency-Key replay body-match check as 'byte-identical'
summary: The actual comparison is sanitize_pg_text(stored) == sanitize_pg_text(new) — sanitize_pg_text normalizes invalid UTF-8/embedded NULs, so literal byte-identity was never the real contract. Two independent reporters (strongest-confirmed SHOULD in this run). Reworded to 'identical after sanitization'.

trigger: Whether an idempotent replay should re-fire audit+emit or silently skip it
summary: Already adjudicated by the human operator via AskUserQuestion during the original design phase ('re-fire audit+emit on replay', the Recommended option) before this session's implementation began. Not re-litigated.

The original 10-entry unhappy-path risk register's remaining entries (R5, R7, R9, R10) were reported as MEDIUM/LOW/N-A tier alongside chaos-injector scenario suggestions, but their exact text was not preserved in this session's context after a mid-run compaction. Not re-derived or fabricated here. Recoverable from the session transcript per this repo's 'Gov transcript recovery' convention if a future reviewer needs the specifics; none of them were flagged as BLOCKING at the time.
waiver_rationale: transcript-recovery deferred; none were reported BLOCKING

trigger: yuzu_server_product_pack_install_compensation_total not pre-seeded at boot, unlike its two sibling counters
summary: Fixed: describe() + zero-loop pre-seed for both ok/partial values. Empirically proven load-bearing (not just convention) via promtool test rules: increase() cannot detect a 0->1 step on a series whose first-ever sample is already 1.

trigger: items_to_store can carry the same item_id twice (the duplicate-item-id detection case)
summary: compensate_and_fail called compensate_fn twice for the same item_id, manufacturing a false partial result/metric for content never actually orphaned. Fixed with a dedup set — later found itself defective (see gate8-security-cross-kind-dedup below) and re-fixed.
disposition: fixed, then superseded by a corrected fix (see cross-kind finding)

trigger: No test wired set_metrics before forcing a partial compensation
summary: The compensated==attempted label-selection logic (the exact code the dedup fix touched) had zero unit coverage of its metric-emission side effect. Fixed with a dedicated test asserting both ok and partial series increment correctly.

trigger: metrics.md said 'Alert on a sustained non-zero partial rate' but the shipped rule fires on any single occurrence (for:0m)
summary: Two independent reporters (docs-writer and sre, converging on the same fix). Reworded to 'any occurrence'; sre additionally verified via promtool that the alert's any-occurrence semantics are correctly implemented.

trigger: Two documents of DIFFERENT kind sharing the same attacker-chosen item_id (PolicyFragment + Policy, via a caller-supplied id: field PolicyStore honors verbatim)
summary: The architect-recommended item_id-only dedup (gate8-architect-double-compensation-dedup) was itself defective: it silently skipped compensating the second, different-kind item sharing the id, reporting a real orphan as fully compensated. VERIFIED with a live repro (temp test wired a real PolicyStore, confirmed the orphan, reverted the repro). Fixed by keying the dedup on (kind, item_id) instead, matching compensate_fn's own dispatch identity. Independently re-verified closed via a negative-control repro (reverting the fix reproduces the exact original test failure).

trigger: The (kind,item_id) dedup key concatenates with a '\x1f' separator
summary: Safe today because item.kind can only ever be one of 4 hardcoded literals (never containing 0x1F), verified via install_fn's exact-string dispatch; item_id CAN carry an embedded 0x1F byte, but a collision requires 0x1F inside a kind string, which cannot happen today. Speculative, no reachable trigger — recorded, not fixed (would need a future kind name derived from caller input to matter).
waiver_rationale: speculative, no reachable trigger; a pair-keyed set would remove the class structurally at low cost if ever revisited

trigger: R1 (cross-pack fragment coupling) existed only as prose in a non-terminal commit message, no filed issue
summary: Verified empirically: gh issue search found 0 hits, no doc references it, no governance.d/3481-*.jsonl existed yet (run was still in flight). CC7.2 change-management traceability gap. Resolved by this ledger entry (gate4-r1-cross-pack-fragment-coupling) plus a drafted (not yet filed) issue, condition explicitly carried to the consolidated operator checkpoint.

trigger: A denied install's audit detail carried no compensation outcome (N/M count)
summary: An auditor reconstructing purely from the audit store couldn't tell whether compensation fully/partially succeeded. Fixed: error_message gains a '(compensated N/M item(s))' suffix whenever a compensation attempt actually ran; rest-api.md and audit-log.md updated to match.

trigger: A process crash/restart during the compensation loop, including immediately after its last successful iteration
summary: Metric/log/audit are all written only AFTER the compensation loop completes; a crash mid-loop leaves NO evidence on any of the three channels for that specific attempt. Not a regression versus pre-PR (same absent observability existed for the original silent-orphan bug) but an incompletely-closed gap. Documented as an explicit operator-facing blind spot (product_pack_store.hpp + metrics.md) rather than code-fixed this round; a fast-follow (increment the metric at the FIRST failed item rather than after the loop) was scoped but explicitly NOT implemented, since it would re-open the Gate 8 promtool-verified emission-point ground for a marginal robustness gain.
waiver_rationale: the fix is more invasive than proportionate to the marginal risk reduction; documented instead per explicit sre recommendation option (b)

trigger: Retry after a partial compensation failure, where the residual item is a PolicyFragment (unconditional name collision) or any kind with a retry-stable explicit id
provenance: mixed (pre-existing per-document swallow + this PR's compensation is the but-for cause of reaching it on retry)
summary: Traced end to end against live code (PolicyStore's unconditional duplicate-name check, id_val.empty()?generate_id():id_val, create_policy's fragment-id lookup, the pre-existing per-document error-tolerant loop, the 201 response's lack of an errors field) and verified accurate. The retry's own re-creation of the residual document fails and is silently swallowed into an aggregate error count invisible to the caller; any cross-reference to it (e.g. a Policy's spec.fragment) resolves against the stale orphan. The real fix (surface per-item errors in the response, OR make the whole install all-or-nothing on any post-loop failure) changes pre-existing API semantics beyond this PR's scope and is NOT decided unilaterally, per this PR's own handover-doc mandate to present design decisions rather than silently pick one. What WAS fixed this round: the changelog's factually WRONG characterization of the outcome as 'duplicate content' (true for some kinds, false for this one) was corrected to name both outcomes precisely.
classification: truth, enterprise-readiness owns customer-facing readiness; disposition is architect/operator territory
disposition: fixed — operator chose option (a) (2026-08-24, "1 - a"): install() gains a partial_result out-param, workflow_routes.cpp's POST handler surfaces per-item errors/installed_count/total_items in the response body and the failed/total count in the audit detail. Also closes the pre-existing #3479 this option subsumes.

trigger: YuzuProductPackCompensationPartial self-resolves after ~1h while the orphan does not self-heal, and the alert's own description didn't say so
summary: metrics.md correctly stated this nuance, but that's read once at setup, not at the moment an on-call engineer triages a firing alert. Fixed: added the auto-resolve caveat directly to the alert's own annotations.description.

trigger: A network fault landing between Postgres processing COMMIT and the client reading PGRES_COMMAND_OK
summary: with_txn_for's single bool return could not distinguish 'transaction never started' from 'connection held, ambiguous ack loss after a genuine commit' -- compensating on the latter would actively delete real, already-persisted content. Fixed via PgPool::with_txn_on (new public wrapper) + a fresh server-authoritative outcome check before compensating on any lease-held failure. Superseded in its exact mechanism by CHAOS-1b (row-visibility replaced with pg_xact_status) but the original acquire-vs-held-lease distinction remains load-bearing.

trigger: The CHAOS-1 fix's own existence re-check races an in-flight commit -- a client-observed connection failure is not ordered relative to backend commit progress
summary: check_pack_row_exists assumed any observed commit failure was already settled server-side; a middlebox/pooler-severed connection can be observed by the client before the backend finishes applying an already-in-flight commit, so a fresh read could see kAbsent for a transaction that is not aborted, merely not-yet-committed -- the identical destructive-deletion hazard through a different door. Fixed: replaced with check_transaction_outcome using Postgres's own pg_xact_status(), the server-authoritative answer documented for exactly this scenario. Independently re-verified CLOSED by a second security-guardian pass; the review explicitly found no CHAOS-1c -- every residual ambiguity (still-in-progress, too-old-for-commit-log, check-itself-unreachable) degrades to the same safe skip-compensation arm.

trigger: A large duplicate-item-id bundle forcing ~2N synchronous, unbounded-timeout sibling-store lock acquisitions on one HTTP worker thread
provenance: mixed (install_fn's own N-pass loop is pre-existing/unchanged by this PR; compensate_fn's SECOND N-pass on the duplicate-item-id path is this PR's own contribution)
summary: Reported with an explicit provenance caveat by chaos-injector itself, matching the same pre-existing-vs-amplified split as R1. Not fixed this round -- flagged for the operator's disposition alongside R1 rather than silently deferred, consistent with this run's overall discriminator (does the wrong outcome traverse code this diff added?).
classification: truth, chaos-injector owns failure-mode discovery; disposition is operator territory given the mixed provenance

trigger: Same as gate4-r3
summary: Independently re-derived by chaos-injector as a narrower reading of the Gate 4 finding; same fix (gate4-r3) covers it. Also proven live and end-to-end by the CHAOS-1b integration test, which doubles as this scenario's regression net.

trigger: A bundle placing a Workflow document before the InstructionDefinition it references
provenance: introduced (doc claim) / pre-existing (WorkflowEngine's own missing check)
summary: The reverse-compensation-order safety argument is PolicyStore-specific and silently assumed to generalize; WorkflowEngine::create_workflow has no equivalent existence check, so out-of-dependency-order bundles produce a brief, self-healing window where a Workflow row points at an already-compensated InstructionDefinition. Fixed via doc: scoped the reverse-order rationale explicitly to PolicyStore and named the WorkflowEngine gap rather than adding sibling-store code.

trigger: compensate_fn throws AFTER its underlying delete already committed
summary: A safe-direction false positive (reported as compensation FAILED for content that's actually clean) rather than a false negative -- confirmatory, not actionable. No fix required; accepted as-is.
waiver_rationale: safe-direction false positive, not a defect

trigger: PgPool::with_txn_on's public exposure has no documented/enforced idle-transaction precondition on the caller-supplied lease
summary: Previously structurally impossible via the private run_in_txn (only ever fed a fresh lease from acquire()/try_acquire_for()); now a future misuse could pass an already-dirty lease. No live trigger -- speculative. Fixed via a strengthened doxygen precondition (three explicit rules) rather than a runtime guard, matching architect's own recommendation that documentation-only is proportionate for a single-call-site escape hatch.

trigger: with_txn_on's bounded-acquire discipline is on the caller, not the call, unlike with_txn_for
summary: Nothing BLOCKING per architect's own review; ADR-0012 §3's 'never expose their lease' clause does not apply (direction is inverted -- the pool accepting back a lease the SAME caller already acquired via the pool's own public API, not a store exposing its lease outward). Fixed: strengthened docstring + a one-line mention in postgres-store-playbook.md's anti-patterns list so a future store author discovers the pattern.

trigger: install()'s per-document error-tolerant loop drops per-item failure detail on both partial and total failure (pre-existing #3479), which gate6-enterprise-f1 showed is what lets a compensation-triggered retry silently drop content while reporting 201
provenance: pre-existing (#3479), newly-reachable via this PR's compensation mechanism
summary: install() gains a trailing InstallPartialResult* partial_result out-param (default null, byte-unchanged behavior for every existing caller). Populated on every install_fn-driven outcome. The all-failed 400 now joins every document's reason (not just errors[0]). The POST /api/product-packs response body gains errors/installed_count/total_items on a genuine partial success; the audit success row's detail names the failed/total count. Closes #3479 directly (operator-chosen disposition (a) for gate6-enterprise-f1).
classification: truth, fixed per explicit operator direction

trigger: A document's YAML field value (e.g. mode:) reflected into an install_fn error string contains invalid UTF-8
summary: The new partial-success response body's nlohmann::json::dump() defaulted to strict UTF-8 validation and could throw AFTER the partial install and its audit row already committed, returning an empty 500 to the caller (single-request unavailability only, no crash, no data risk). No information-disclosure finding on the errors[] surfacing itself -- confirmed the same message class was already exposed via the pre-existing all-failed 400 and the direct per-store REST endpoints. Fixed with error_handler_t::replace, the established repo convention. Verified with a negative control: reverting to plain dump() reproduces the exact json.exception.type_error.316 the new test asserts against.

trigger: Gate 1's Resource Ledger omitted the idempotency pre-check's own Lease + PgResult acquisition
summary: Policy-floor finding: an owning raw-resource boundary present in the diff but absent from the Resource Ledger is BLOCKING regardless of code safety, per cpp-safety's own charter. Verified safe by inspection (stack-scoped RAII, released on every path). Corrected in this run's own Gate 1 summary text (conversational, not a committed artifact) rather than a code change.
waiver_rationale: code verified safe; the floor is about ledger completeness, which is corrected in-run

trigger: InstallPartialResult's doc comment claims population on both outcomes, but compensate_and_fail's two call sites never called populate_partial_result()
summary: Fixed: populate_partial_result() now called as compensate_and_fail's first statement (covers both call sites: duplicate-item-id, final-persist kAborted fall-through) and added to the kUnknown branch. Every semantic exit from install() now populates exactly once.

trigger: The alert description and metrics.md gave ONE remediation instruction for two different partial-result shapes (confirmed orphan vs ambiguous-outcome)
summary: An operator following the old uniform guidance on the ambiguous-outcome shape (no item named) could reconstruct ids from the submitted bundle and delete LIVE, successfully-installed content -- the exact destructive hazard CHAOS-1/1b closed in code, reintroduced at the runbook level. Fixed both docs to require reading the log line first and explicitly forbid guessing ids for the ambiguous shape, directing the operator to GET /api/product-packs/{id} instead.

trigger: The kUnknown branch's metric increment was gated only on metrics_ != nullptr, unlike compensate_and_fail's own increment (gated on compensate_fn) and unlike the counter's own description
summary: No live discrepancy today (only production caller always supplies compensate_fn). Fixed to gate on compensate_fn too, matching the sibling emission site's semantics.

trigger: hpp comment claimed a total-failure install never touches Postgres at all, now false for a keyed install (F033 pre-check runs one read)
summary: Fixed: reworded to 'never WRITES to Postgres' with an explicit note about the F033 pre-check's read.
classification: wording, cpp-expert flagged a truth issue in a comment; docs-writer-shaped fix

trigger: install()'s TransactionOutcome switch's kCommitted and kUnknown arms have no install()-level integration coverage -- only kAborted is driven end-to-end
summary: check_transaction_outcome itself is unit-tested for all three outcomes at the seam; the switch's WIRING inside install() for kCommitted/kUnknown is only reachable via real network-fault injection, unavailable in this suite -- already honestly disclosed in the branch's own comments/commit messages as `likely` not `verified`. Accepted as an explicitly-disclosed limitation rather than a refactor (making check_transaction_outcome injectable) at this stage; a fast-follow candidate, not fixed this round.
waiver_rationale: already honestly disclosed as likely-not-verified in the branch's own text; a seam-injection refactor is disproportionate at this stage of an already-extensive PR

trigger: promtool CASE 67's name/comment said 'pre-seed pinned' but the case verifies the RULE given a synthetic pre-seeded series, not that server.cpp's own pre-seed loop ran at boot
summary: Fixed: renamed/reworded to accurately describe what the case verifies; noted the same gap (no C++ test exercises the pre-seed loop itself) already exists for the pre-existing sibling counters, not a new regression.
